Powers and functions of board.—(1) The board may exercise all such powers as may be necessary or expedient for the purpose of carrying out its functions under this Act. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, such powers shall include the power— (a) to admit members; 1[(aa) to elect the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson or President and Vice-President of the multi-State co-operative society from amongst the elected members of the board in accordance with the directions of the Authority: Provided that the certificate of election shall be issued by the Chief Executive of the multi-State co-operative society after conclusion of resolution by the board;] (b) to interpret the organisational objectives and set-up specific goals to be achieved towards these objectives; (c) to make periodic appraisal of operations; (d) to appoint and remove a Chief Executive and such other employees of the society as are not required to be appointed by the Chief Executive; (e) to make provisions for regulating the appointment of employees of the multi-State co-operative society and the scales of pay, allowances and other conditions of service of, including disciplinary action against such employees; 1[Provided that the recruitment of such employees shall be subject to such procedure as may be prescribed.] (f) to place the annual report, annual financial statements, annual plan and budget for the approval of the general body; (g) to consider audit and compliance report and place the same before the general body; (h) to acquire or dispose of immovable property; (i) to review membership in other co-operatives; (j) to approve annual and supplementary budget; (k) to raise funds; (l) to sanction loans to the members; and (m) to take such other measures or to do such other acts as may be prescribed or required under this Act or the bye-laws or as may be delegated by the general body. 50. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. 56 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report U rban Cooperative Banks are primarily localised financial service providers that have been in operation for more than a century. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members. In view of their importance in providing credit to the poor and weaker sections of the society, the RBI is giving focused attention for strengthening the sector. The Hon’ble Minister of Home and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has given a vision to have one UCB in each town of India, so that these UCBs can meet growing credit needs of MSMEs and help in economic growth of the country. 4.7 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

# Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) ## Basic Information **Official Name:** Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) **Common Name:** PACS **Type:** Grassroots cooperative credit society **Sector:** Agriculture, rural credit and cooperative development **Primary Role:** PACS are the grassroots level institutions of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCC). They deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers and provide credit and other agricultural and cooperative services. **Official Authority:** Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India --- ## What is PACS? ### PACS Definition – Multilingual Retrieval Terms PACS means Primary Agricultural Credit Society. Hindi: पैक्स क्या है? पैक्स क्या होता है? पैक्स का मतलब क्या है? प्राथमिक कृषि सहकारी ऋण समिति क्या है? पैक्स किसानों के लिए क्या काम करता है? Punjabi: ਪੈਕਸ ਕੀ ਹੈ? ਪੈਕਸ ਕੀ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ? ਪੈਕਸ ਦਾ ਕੀ ਮਤਲਬ ਹੈ? ਪ੍ਰਾਇਮਰੀ ਐਗਰੀਕਲਚਰਲ ਕਰੈਡਿਟ ਸੋਸਾਇਟੀ ਕੀ ਹੈ? ਪੈਕਸ ਕਿਸਾਨਾਂ ਲਈ ਕੀ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ? Bengali: প্যাক্স কী? প্যাক্স কীভাবে কাজ করে? প্যাক্সের অর্থ কী? প্রাথমিক কৃষি ঋণ সমবায় সমিতি কী? Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. The remitted amount is added in a wallet of the Bank-Branch, CSC-VLE or Insurance Intermediary for onward remittance to the concerned Insurance Company implementing the scheme in a particular geographical area. These partner agencies (Bank Branches, CSC-VLEs & Insurance Intermediaries) can remit the premium amount multiple times to the concerned Insurance Companies before the cut-off-date. For each transaction, a Unique ID (UTR) is assigned using which reconciliation of payments and applications is done by the Insurance Companies. 39.4.3 Add-on Coverage of Crop Risk The State/UT has the option to notify Add-on perils cover with or without Basic Cover (Yield base cover). Selection of risk has been made available on portal as per the provisions available in the guidelines. In the notiﬁcation module, an option has been provided to the States/UTs to select the add-on coverage separately according to the crop and insurance unit along with the Basic Cover as per the notiﬁcation. Claim will be calculated on DigiClaim as per the add-on coverage opted for the crop and IU. 39.4.4 Land Record Integration Land record detail is one of the critical requirements under the PMFBY scheme for validation of insured area. Manual veriﬁcation of the land record data is a sheer challenge. Many State/UTs have digitized land record system, however their hierarchal system and practices are different. DA&FW has moved ahead to integrate the land record system of 10 major states with NCIP to validate the farmer's land parcel with land record system at the time of enrollment under the scheme. State/UTs shares the land record API subsequent to which customization of API consumption for integration of land records of the State(s) with NCIP is executed. The land record details of the farmers is required to be entered during enrolment process and rest of the land details viz. extent of land, ownership share and names of owners/shareholders are fetched through the State/UT land record portal. In the Future, as and when the Agri-Stack system becomes operational, the farmer’s Golden ID along with land records, land area, cadastral maps and sown crop details shall be fetched & validated using it. 39.4.5 Location Master Management

It is a Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra operated by a Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS). ### Can PACS open Jan Aushadhi Kendras? Yes. PACS can be allowed to open and operate Jan Aushadhi Kendras subject to the applicable Government procedures and conditions. ### Why are Jan Aushadhi Kendras being promoted through PACS? The initiative improves access to affordable medicines in rural areas and provides PACS with an additional economic activity. ### What are the benefits for PACS? PACS operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras can receive applicable trade margins and incentives under the PMBJP framework, subject to current guidelines. ### How many Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been opened through PACS? top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. # Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) ## Basic Information **Official Name:** Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) **Common Name:** PACS **Type:** Grassroots cooperative credit society **Sector:** Agriculture, rural credit and cooperative development **Primary Role:** PACS are the grassroots level institutions of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCC). They deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers and provide credit and other agricultural and cooperative services. **Official Authority:** Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India --- ## What is PACS? ### PACS Definition – Multilingual Retrieval Terms PACS means Primary Agricultural Credit Society. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. To bring in efficiency, accountability, transparency at PACS and improve profitability. b. To bring in accuracy and uniformity in the conduct of business, accounting with

top3.source: ministry_of_cooperation\Revised Scheme guidelines (Computerization of PACS project).pdf
top3.text: 4 entries originating at the transaction level and reporting thereof through standardization of processes, implementation of Common Accounting System (CAS) and Management Information System (MIS) and compliance to stipulations. c. To transform PACS into multi service entities, offering to members in particular and the rural population in general, an array of services covering agriculture and allied activities; financial and non-financial products. d. To seamlessly connect PACS with the higher-tier institutions and Government departments in the domains of agriculture, banking and rural development for dissemination of knowledge to grassroots. e. To leverage on the unique strength of PACS i.e. their captive member base, to design and offer personalized products and services and thereby improve the socio-economic landscape of rural India. f. To ensure accurate delivery of funds and subsidies through DBT to the targeted beneficiary groups. g. To enable PACS to provide doorstep banking services to facilitate easier access to banking services. h. To enable PACS to utilize digital acceptance infrastructure like Point of Sale (POS)/ mobile POS (mPoS)/ QR Code Readers/Green Pin solution /BHIM Aadhaar pay device, etc. in the establishments run by PACS like fertilizer shops, Seed Processing units, etc. to facilitate cashless/digital transactions. i. To expand financial services to unbanked villages / areas, improve the overall performance and efficiency of PACS and STCCS, increase rural employment opportunities and reduce migration to urban areas. 3 Project Details 3.1 Title of the Project Centrally Sponsored Project for ‘Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies’. 3.2 Sponsoring Agency Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India. 3.3 Duration of the Project For a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27.

top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. PACS form the grassroots level of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. The higher levels include: 1. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) 2. District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) 3. State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) NABARD supports and refinances the cooperative credit system through the higher cooperative banking structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. --- ## Who Can Become a PACS Member? Membership of a PACS is governed by the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, rules and the society's bye-laws. Therefore, there is no single universal membership rule or document list that applies identically to every PACS in India. A person interested in joining a PACS should check: * The applicable State cooperative law * The PACS bye-laws * The membership eligibility conditions * The local PACS office * Any required membership or share contribution * Documents required by the concerned PACS SIA should avoid giving a fixed list of membership documents unless the relevant State/PACS rules have been verified. --- ## How Can I Join a PACS? A general process may involve: 1. Identify the relevant PACS in the person's area. 2. Check its applicable membership eligibility rules. 3. Obtain the membership application/form from the PACS or its designated channel. 4. Submit the required information and documents. 5. Complete any required share contribution or membership formalities. 6. Wait for approval according to the applicable cooperative rules and bye-laws. The exact process can vary by State and PACS. For a specific membership question, SIA should ask for the user's State or location before giving detailed eligibility or document guidance. --- ## Can PACS Give Loans to Farmers? Yes. PACS directly deal with rural and agricultural borrowers and provide credit. PACS traditionally provide short-term and medium-term agricultural credit to member farmers. Loan availability, amount, interest rate, repayment period, collateral requirements and eligibility depend on the applicable rules and the concerned cooperative credit institution. SIA should verify current loan conditions before giving specific financial figures. --- ## What Agricultural Inputs Can PACS Provide? PACS may provide or distribute agricultural inputs such as: * Seeds * Fertilizers * Pesticides They may also provide other agricultural services depending on their activities and applicable rules. --- ## Can PACS Provide Storage Services? Yes. PACS can undertake storage and warehousing-related activities. The Model Bye-laws support diversification of PACS into activities such as godowns, warehousing and food-grain procurement. Individual availability depends on the PACS, local implementation and applicable permissions. --- ## Can PACS Function as Common Service Centres? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has enabled PACS to function as Common Service Centres

36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) 3. State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) NABARD supports and refinances the cooperative credit system through the higher cooperative banking structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. --- ## Who Can Become a PACS Member? Membership of a PACS is governed by the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, rules and the society's bye-laws. Therefore, there is no single universal membership rule or document list that applies identically to every PACS in India. A person interested in joining a PACS should check: * The applicable State cooperative law * The PACS bye-laws * The membership eligibility conditions * The local PACS office * Any required membership or share contribution * Documents required by the concerned PACS SIA should avoid giving a fixed list of membership documents unless the relevant State/PACS rules have been verified. --- ## How Can I Join a PACS? A general process may involve: 1. Identify the relevant PACS in the person's area. 2. Check its applicable membership eligibility rules. 3. Obtain the membership application/form from the PACS or its designated channel. 4. Submit the required information and documents. 5. Complete any required share contribution or membership formalities. 6. Wait for approval according to the applicable cooperative rules and bye-laws. The exact process can vary by State and PACS. For a specific membership question, SIA should ask for the user's State or location before giving detailed eligibility or document guidance. --- ## Can PACS Give Loans to Farmers? Yes. PACS directly deal with rural and agricultural borrowers and provide credit. PACS traditionally provide short-term and medium-term agricultural credit to member farmers. Loan availability, amount, interest rate, repayment period, collateral requirements and eligibility depend on the applicable rules and the concerned cooperative credit institution. SIA should verify current loan conditions before giving specific financial figures. --- ## What Agricultural Inputs Can PACS Provide? PACS may provide or distribute agricultural inputs such as: * Seeds * Fertilizers * Pesticides They may also provide other agricultural services depending on their activities and applicable rules. --- ## Can PACS Provide Storage Services? top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. To bring in efficiency, accountability, transparency at PACS and improve profitability. b. To bring in accuracy and uniformity in the conduct of business, accounting with

credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. SIA should not give a fixed loan amount or interest rate unless it has a verified current official source. --- ## How Does PACS Connect With NABARD and Cooperative Banks? PACS form the grassroots level of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. The higher levels include: 1. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) 2. District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) 3. State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) NABARD supports and refinances the cooperative credit system through the higher cooperative banking structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. --- ## Who Can Become a PACS Member? Membership of a PACS is governed by the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, rules and the society's bye-laws. Therefore, there is no single universal membership rule or document list that applies identically to every PACS in India. A person interested in joining a PACS should check: * The applicable State cooperative law * The PACS bye-laws * The membership eligibility conditions * The local PACS office * Any required membership or share contribution * Documents required by the concerned PACS SIA should avoid giving a fixed list of membership documents unless the relevant State/PACS rules have been verified. --- ## How Can I Join a PACS? A general process may involve: 1. Identify the relevant PACS in the person's area. 2. Check its applicable membership eligibility rules. 3. Obtain the membership application/form from the PACS or its designated channel. 4. Submit the required information and documents. 5. Complete any required share contribution or membership formalities. 6. Wait for approval according to the applicable cooperative rules and bye-laws. The exact process can vary by State and PACS. For a specific membership question, SIA should ask for the user's State or location before giving detailed eligibility or document guidance. --- ## Can PACS Give Loans to Farmers? Yes. PACS directly deal with rural and agricultural borrowers and provide credit. PACS traditionally provide short-term and medium-term agricultural credit to member farmers. Loan availability, amount, interest rate, repayment period, collateral requirements and eligibility depend on the applicable rules and the concerned cooperative credit institution. SIA should verify current loan conditions before giving specific financial figures. --- ## What Agricultural Inputs Can PACS Provide? PACS may provide or distribute agricultural inputs such as: * Seeds * Fertilizers * Pesticides They may also provide other agricultural services depending on their activities and applicable rules. --- ## Can PACS Provide Storage Services? Yes. PACS can undertake storage and warehousing-related activities. The Model Bye-laws support diversification of PACS into activities such as godowns, warehousing and food-grain procurement. Individual availability depends on the PACS, local implementation and applicable permissions. --- ## Can PACS Function as Common Service Centres? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has enabled PACS to function as Common Service Centres

top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. To bring in efficiency, accountability, transparency at PACS and improve profitability. b. To bring in accuracy and uniformity in the conduct of business, accounting with

To transform PACS into multi service entities, offering to members in particular and the rural population in general, an array of services covering agriculture and allied activities; financial and non-financial products. d. To seamlessly connect PACS with the higher-tier institutions and Government departments in the domains of agriculture, banking and rural development for dissemination of knowledge to grassroots. e. To leverage on the unique strength of PACS i.e. their captive member base, to design and offer personalized products and services and thereby improve the socio-economic landscape of rural India. f. To ensure accurate delivery of funds and subsidies through DBT to the targeted beneficiary groups. g. To enable PACS to provide doorstep banking services to facilitate easier access to banking services. h. To enable PACS to utilize digital acceptance infrastructure like Point of Sale (POS)/ mobile POS (mPoS)/ QR Code Readers/Green Pin solution /BHIM Aadhaar pay device, etc. in the establishments run by PACS like fertilizer shops, Seed Processing units, etc. to facilitate cashless/digital transactions. i. To expand financial services to unbanked villages / areas, improve the overall performance and efficiency of PACS and STCCS, increase rural employment opportunities and reduce migration to urban areas. 3 Project Details 3.1 Title of the Project Centrally Sponsored Project for ‘Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies’. 3.2 Sponsoring Agency Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India. 3.3 Duration of the Project For a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27.

The Ministry of Cooperation has enabled PACS to function as Common Service Centres (CSCs). Through the CSC framework, PACS can provide various e-governance and citizen-centric services. These can include services related to: * Banking * Insurance * Aadhaar enrolment or updation * Health services * Agricultural services * Government welfare schemes * Other permitted digital services The exact services available at a particular PACS may vary. --- ## Can PACS Become Multipurpose Cooperative Societies? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has prepared Model Bye-laws to help PACS diversify their activities and become multipurpose cooperative societies. The Model Bye-laws enable PACS to undertake more than 25 types of business activities across areas such as agriculture, dairy, fisheries, storage, retail and citizen services. Adoption and implementation are subject to the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act and State-level requirements. --- ## PACS Computerization The Government of India approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS in June 2022. The project aims to bring functional PACS onto an ERP-based common software system and connect them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks. The computerization initiative aims to: * Improve operational efficiency * Speed up loan disbursal * Reduce transaction costs * Improve accounting * Increase transparency * Improve coordination with DCCBs and StCBs --- ## PACS and Farmer Services PACS can act as a local point for farmers to access: * Agricultural credit * Agricultural inputs * Storage facilities * Marketing-related services * Government schemes * Digital citizen services * Other cooperative services The exact services available depend on the PACS and applicable schemes or permissions. --- ## Important Limitation for SIA PACS are governed by applicable cooperative laws and bye-laws. Individual availability depends on the PACS, local implementation and applicable permissions. --- ## Can PACS Function as Common Service Centres? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has enabled PACS to function as Common Service Centres (CSCs). Through the CSC framework, PACS can provide various e-governance and citizen-centric services. These can include services related to: * Banking * Insurance * Aadhaar enrolment or updation * Health services * Agricultural services * Government welfare schemes * Other permitted digital services The exact services available at a particular PACS may vary. --- ## Can PACS Become Multipurpose Cooperative Societies? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has prepared Model Bye-laws to help PACS diversify their activities and become multipurpose cooperative societies. The Model Bye-laws enable PACS to undertake more than 25 types of business activities across areas such as agriculture, dairy, fisheries, storage, retail and citizen services. Adoption and implementation are subject to the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act and State-level requirements. --- ## PACS Computerization The Government of India approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS in June 2022. The project aims to bring functional PACS onto an ERP-based common software system and connect them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks. The computerization initiative aims to: * Improve operational efficiency * Speed up loan disbursal * Reduce transaction costs * Improve accounting * Increase transparency * Improve coordination with DCCBs and StCBs --- ## PACS and Farmer Services PACS can act as a local point for farmers to access: * Agricultural credit * Agricultural inputs * Storage facilities * Marketing-related services * Government schemes * Digital citizen services * Other cooperative services The exact services available depend on the PACS and applicable schemes or permissions. --- ## Important Limitation for SIA PACS are governed by applicable cooperative laws and bye-laws. SIA should not assume that every PACS provides every possible service. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. # Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) ## Basic Information **Official Name:** Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) **Common Name:** PACS **Type:** Grassroots cooperative credit society **Sector:** Agriculture, rural credit and cooperative development **Primary Role:** PACS are the grassroots level institutions of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCC). They deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers and provide credit and other agricultural and cooperative services. **Official Authority:** Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India --- ## What is PACS? ### PACS Definition – Multilingual Retrieval Terms PACS means Primary Agricultural Credit Society. Hindi: पैक्स क्या है? पैक्स क्या होता है? पैक्स का मतलब क्या है? प्राथमिक कृषि सहकारी ऋण समिति क्या है? पैक्स किसानों के लिए क्या काम करता है? Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. results.retrieved_text: 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

results.retrieved_text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). A cooperative is an autonomous association of persons, united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social, and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly owned and democratically member-controlled enterprise. 1.2. India has more than 8 lakh cooperative societies, comprising around 2 lakh credit cooperatives and 6 lakh non-credit cooperatives. Non- credit cooperatives primarily operate in sectors such as housing, dairy, labour, and others, including sugar, consumer, marketing, fisheries, textiles, services, processing, hospitals, etc. Moreover, with about 30 crore total members in the cooperative sector, PACS alone have more than 13 crore members spread across the country. 1.3. The last policy on cooperatives, released in 2002, focused on the basic dimensions of efficiently organizing economic activities by cooperatives. Over the last 20 years, the world has witnessed radical changes at individual, societal, national, and global levels. They have been driven by globalization and technological advancements, especially in communications and information technology. Given these developments, it became essential to revisit the policy and formulate a new one to suit the evolving requirements of the cooperative sector and to ensure the sustainability of this sector in the current economic scenario. 1.4. Recognizing the formation of cooperative societies as a fundamental right under the Constitution of India and the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation marked a new era. This era requires transformation of the cooperative movement with “farmers, women and rural development” at its centre, along with strengthening cooperative societies, making national federations lead the way, and ensuring both Central and State Governments provide the needed support and recognition for these institutions to grow. Hence, there is an urgent need for a new national policy. 1.5. The vision of ‘Sahkar-Se-Samriddhi’ as articulated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India gives an endearing message motivating the stakeholders and instilling confidence in the sector. It has motivated the Ministry and the cooperative sector to work together towards achieving the above vision.

DEFINITION OF A COOPERATIVE A cooperative is an autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly-owned and democratically-controlled enterprise. COOPERATIVE VALUES Cooperatives are based on the values of self-help, self-responsibility, democracy, equality, equity, and solidarity. In the tradition of their founders, cooperative members believe in the ethical values of honesty, openness, social responsibility and caring for others. COOPERATIVE PRINCIPLES The cooperative principles are guidelines by which cooperatives put their values into practice. 1. Voluntary and Open Membership Cooperatives are voluntary organisations, open to all persons able to use their services and willing to accept the responsibilities of membership, without gender, social, racial, political or religious discrimination. 2. Democratic Member Control Cooperatives are democratic organisations controlled by their members, who actively participate in setting their policies and making decisions. Men and women serving as elected representatives are accountable to the membership. In primary cooperatives members have equal voting rights (one member, one vote) and cooperatives at other levels are also organised in a democratic manner. 3. Member Economic Participation Members contribute equitably to, and democratically control, the capital of their cooperative. At least part of that capital is usually the common property of the cooperative. Members usually receive limited compensation, if any, on capital subscribed as a condition of membership. Members allocate surpluses for any or all of the following purposes: developing their cooperative, possibly by setting up reserves, part of which at least would be indivisible, benefiting members in proportion to their transactions with the cooperative, and supporting other activities approved by the membership. 4. Autonomy and Independence Cooperatives are autonomous, self-help organisations controlled by their members. If they enter into agreements with other organisations, including governments, or raise capital from external sources, they do so on terms that ensure democratic control by their members and maintain their cooperative autonomy. 5. Education, Training, and Information Cooperatives provide education and training for their members, elected representatives, managers, end employees so they can contribute effectively to the development of their cooperatives. They inform the general public - particularly young people and opinion leaders about the nature and benefits of co- operation. 6. Cooperation among Cooperatives Cooperatives serve their members most effectively and strengthen the cooperative movement by working together through local, national, regional and international structures. 7. Concern for Community Cooperatives work for the sustainable development of their communities through policies approved by their members.

3 Background I. Cooperation is embedded in the fabric of Indian society, which drives the spirit of collaboration to achieve common socio-economic goals. II. Cooperativism is a socio-economic system based on collective participation, democratic members’ control, and shared benefits, where individuals voluntarily unite to form cooperatives for mutual support and economic development. It embodies a synergistic approach—leveraging the efficiency, innovation, and market dynamism while championing the equity, inclusivity, and social welfare principles. This fusion offers a strong alternative to the current economic systems, providing a model that prioritizes both economic growth and collective well-being. III. India is home to more than one-fourth of the world's cooperatives, with about one- third of its rural population directly connected to them as members for their diverse socio-economic needs. IV. The Indian cooperative movement has been the flag bearer of a participatory, people-led development model aimed at socio-economic upliftment at the grassroots level for more than a century. Cooperatives in India are guided by core cooperative principles and they are owned by members, operated by members, and for the benefit of members. V. This policy intends to facilitate a systematic and orderly, all-around development of the sector, focused on fast-tracking the growth of the rural economy. 1.8. Since its establishment in 2021, the Ministry of Cooperation has already undertaken several initiatives to fulfil the above vision. Major initiatives include: a) Strengthening of cooperative societies i. New model by-laws to make PACS multipurpose, ii. SOP (Standard Operating Procedures) launched for the formation of 2 lakh new PACS/dairy/fishery primary cooperatives in uncovered panchayats, iii. SOP launched for cooperative-led “White Revolution 2.0”, iv. Multi-purpose PACS to diversify businesses into non-credit areas, v. World’s largest decentralized grain storage plan at the PACS level, vi. Cooperative societies included as buyers on the GeM portal, etc. b) Cooperation among cooperatives i. Three new multi-state cooperative societies at the national level in the fields of exports, organic products, and seeds, ii. SOP launched for nation-wide implementation of cooperation among cooperatives campaign for primary cooperatives as “Bank Mitra” of cooperative banks, distribution of RuPay KCC to members of primary cooperatives, etc. c) Changes in the Income Tax Act, 1961 for cooperative societies i. Surcharge for societies with income between ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore reduced from 12% to 7%, ii. MAT rate reduced from 18.5% to 15%, iii. Increase in cash withdrawal limit of cooperatives from ₹ 1 crore to ₹ 3 crore without deducting tax at source, etc.

Considering the structure of the cooperative sector, the smooth and effective implementation of the policy requires the active participation of relevant Ministries/Departments of the Central Government, State/UT Governments, and national/state-level cooperative societies/federations/unions. It also involves sectoral development institutions such as NABARD, NCDC, NDDB, and NFDB. 9.3. To ensure the policy is implemented effectively and within a set timeframe, an ‘Implementation Cell’ will be created within the Ministry of Cooperation. This cell will receive support from a dedicated Project Management Unit for technical assistance on the subject, documentation, coordination, monitoring, reporting, and more. 9.4. A detailed action plan, complete with intervention-specific timelines for the implementation of the policy, will be finalized soon after the release of the Policy. 9.5. A ‘National Steering Committee on Cooperation Policy’, chaired by the Union Minister of Cooperation, to be constituted for overall guidance, inter-ministerial coordination, periodic policy review, etc. This committee may include the Hon’ble Minister-in-charge of related Ministries of the Government of India as members, 9.5.2. A national-level ‘Policy Implementation and Monitoring Committee’, chaired by the Union Cooperation Secretary, to be established for central-state coordination, troubleshooting implementation bottlenecks, periodic monitoring and evaluation, etc. It may comprise members, including the Secretary of related Ministries of the Government of India, Secretaries/Principal Secretaries/Additional Chief Secretaries of the Cooperative Department of all States/Union Territories, a representative from NITI Aayog, and Chairpersons/MDs of national cooperative federations/unions/societies, NABARD, NDDB, NCDC, NCCT, VAMNICOM, etc.

5 NATIONAL COOPERATION POLICY 2025 1. Introduction 1.1. A cooperative is an autonomous association of persons, united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social, and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly owned and democratically member-controlled enterprise. 1.2. India has more than 8 lakh cooperative societies, comprising around 2 lakh credit cooperatives and 6 lakh non-credit cooperatives. Non- credit cooperatives primarily operate in sectors such as housing, dairy, labour, and others, including sugar, consumer, marketing, fisheries, textiles, services, processing, hospitals, etc. Moreover, with about 30 crore total members in the cooperative sector, PACS alone have more than 13 crore members spread across the country. 1.3. The last policy on cooperatives, released in 2002, focused on the basic dimensions of efficiently organizing economic activities by cooperatives. Over the last 20 years, the world has witnessed radical changes at individual, societal, national, and global levels. They have been driven by globalization and technological advancements, especially in communications and information technology. Given these developments, it became essential to revisit the policy and formulate a new one to suit the evolving requirements of the cooperative sector and to ensure the sustainability of this sector in the current economic scenario. 1.4. Recognizing the formation of cooperative societies as a fundamental right under the Constitution of India and the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation marked a new era. This era requires transformation of the cooperative movement with “farmers, women and rural development” at its centre, along with strengthening cooperative societies, making national federations lead the way, and ensuring both Central and State Governments provide the needed support and recognition for these institutions to grow. Hence, there is an urgent need for a new national policy. 1.5. The vision of ‘Sahkar-Se-Samriddhi’ as articulated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India gives an endearing message motivating the stakeholders and instilling confidence in the sector. It has motivated the Ministry and the cooperative sector to work together towards achieving the above vision.

Vision, Mission and Objectives Vision: To significantly contribute to India’s collective ambition of becoming ‘Viksit' by 2047 through the promotion of an environment conducive to sustainable cooperative development, following the vision of 'Sahkar-Se-samriddhi'. Mission: To create an enabling legal, economic, and institutional framework that will strengthen and deepen the cooperative movement at the grassroots level and facilitate the transformation of cooperative enterprises into professionally managed, transparent, technology-enabled, vibrant, and responsive economic entities to support production by the masses (members). Promoting Vibrancy: Creating a vibrant and self-sustaining ecosystem. III. Making Cooperatives Future Ready: Transforming cooperatives into professional and sustainable economic entities. IV. Promoting Inclusivity and Deepening Reach: Promoting cooperative-led inclusive development and cooperatives as a people’s movement. V. Entering New and Emerging Sectors: Promoting the entry of cooperatives into new and emerging sectors. VI. Any query or complaint of the farmer will be registered on the NCIP against a unique ticket number. The ticket number will be shared with the farmer through SMS or Chatbot indicating the tentative resolution timeline. Simple queries or complaints shall be resolved by the concerned agent handling the call whereas the serious complaints and grievances which the agents are not able to resolve shall be further forwarded to the concerned Stakeholder viz. results.retrieved_text: / Access Eligible applicants can apply through the applicable State Government agriculture department / designated implementing agency or the official agricultural mechanization platform, according to the current implementation process. The application procedure, documents, machinery list and assistance available may vary by component and State. ## Documents / Information Applicants may be required to provide: - Farmer / beneficiary details - Identity and address information - Land or agricultural activity details, where applicable - Bank account details - Machinery or project details - Other documents required by the implementing agency Exact requirements depend on the component and State-level implementation. ## Frequently Asked Questions / Intents ### What is SMAM? SMAM stands for Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization. It is a government initiative to promote agricultural mechanization and improve farmers' access to modern machinery. ### What is the main purpose of SMAM? The main purpose is to promote the use of agricultural machinery, improve farm efficiency and make modern farm equipment more accessible to farmers. ### Who can benefit from SMAM? Eligible farmers, farmer groups, FPOs, SHGs, cooperatives and other approved beneficiaries can benefit according to applicable guidelines. ### Does SMAM provide financial assistance for farm machinery? Yes. Eligible beneficiaries can receive financial assistance for specified agricultural machinery and equipment subject to applicable conditions. ### What is a Custom Hiring Centre? A Custom Hiring Centre provides agricultural machinery to farmers on a hiring basis, allowing them to use equipment without purchasing it. ### Can small farmers benefit from Custom Hiring Centres? Yes. Custom Hiring Centres can help small and marginal farmers access machinery that may otherwise be expensive to purchase. ### What is a Farm Machinery Bank? A Farm Machinery Bank is a mechanism for providing access to agricultural machinery collectively through eligible groups or organisations. ### Can FPOs benefit from SMAM? Eligible FPOs may benefit from applicable components of the scheme subject to current guidelines. ### Can cooperatives benefit from SMAM? Eligible cooperatives may participate in applicable components subject to the prescribed conditions. ### Where can farmers apply for SMAM? Farmers can apply through the designated State agriculture department / implementing agency or the applicable official agricultural mechanization platform. ### Does SMAM cover all agricultural machinery? No. Only machinery and equipment covered under the applicable scheme components and current guidelines are eligible. ## Important Note SMAM implementation, assistance rates, eligible machinery, beneficiary categories and application procedures may vary according to the current government guidelines and State-level implementation. The application procedure, documents, machinery list and assistance available may vary by component and State. ## Documents / Information Applicants may be required to provide: - Farmer / beneficiary details - Identity and address information - Land or agricultural activity details, where applicable - Bank account details - Machinery or project details - Other documents required by the implementing agency Exact requirements depend on the component and State-level implementation. ## Frequently Asked Questions / Intents ### What is SMAM? SMAM stands for Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization. It is a government initiative to promote agricultural mechanization and improve farmers' access to modern machinery. ### What is the main purpose of SMAM? The main purpose is to promote the use of agricultural machinery, improve farm efficiency and make modern farm equipment more accessible to farmers. ### Who can benefit from SMAM? Eligible farmers, farmer groups, FPOs, SHGs, cooperatives and other approved beneficiaries can benefit according to applicable guidelines. ### Does SMAM provide financial assistance for farm machinery? Yes. Eligible beneficiaries can receive financial assistance for specified agricultural machinery and equipment subject to applicable conditions. ### What is a Custom Hiring Centre? A Custom Hiring Centre provides agricultural machinery to farmers on a hiring basis, allowing them to use equipment without purchasing it. ### Can small farmers benefit from Custom Hiring Centres? Yes. Custom Hiring Centres can help small and marginal farmers access machinery that may otherwise be expensive to purchase. ### What is a Farm Machinery Bank? A Farm Machinery Bank is a mechanism for providing access to agricultural machinery collectively through eligible groups or organisations. ### Can FPOs benefit from SMAM? Eligible FPOs may benefit from applicable components of the scheme subject to current guidelines. ### Can cooperatives benefit from SMAM? Eligible cooperatives may participate in applicable components subject to the prescribed conditions. ### Where can farmers apply for SMAM? Farmers can apply through the designated State agriculture department / implementing agency or the applicable official agricultural mechanization platform. ### Does SMAM cover all agricultural machinery? No. Only machinery and equipment covered under the applicable scheme components and current guidelines are eligible. ## Important Note SMAM implementation, assistance rates, eligible machinery, beneficiary categories and application procedures may vary according to the current government guidelines and State-level implementation. results.retrieved_text: मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

पर भी चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस नोरटस में जनम् नजलजखत सूचनाएं होंगी, अथाातम: (क) जनवााचन द्वारा भरी िाने वाली ररजियों की संख् या ; (ख) जनवााचन का िेत्र (उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट) जिसमें से सिस्ट् यों का जनवााचन दकया िाना है ; (ग) बोडा की सिस्ट् यता की पात्रता हेतु उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट अहाताएं, यदि कोई हैं ; (घ) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी का नाम, तारीख, स्ट् थान और समय जिस िौरान सिस्ट् यों द्वारा नामांकन कागज़ भरा िाएगा, वह तारीख िो जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख से न्द् यूनतम स्ट् पष् ट एक दिन पहले हो या यदि वह एक अवकाि का दिन है तो उससे पूवावती दिन िो सावािजनक अवकाि न हो । स्ट् पष् टीकरण- इस जनयम के प्रयोिन से िब् ि ‘सावािजनक अवकाि’ से ऐसा कोई दिन अजभप्रेत है िो परक्राम् य जलखत अजधजनयम, 1981 (1881 का 26) की धारा 25 के अधीन या ऐसा कोई दिन िो केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार द्वारा, िो भी ििा हो, केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार के कायाालयों के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, सावािजनक अवकाि के ूपप में अजधसूजचत की गई हो ; (ङ) वह तारीख और वह समय और स्ट् थान िब नामांकन कागिों की िांच की िाएगी; और (च) वह तारीख और समय तथा वह स्ट् थान और समय िब मतिान होगा । 19-स. सिस्ट् यों और प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची को तैयार करना - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा उस तारीख के अनुसार िो मतिान के जलए जनयत तारीख से तीस दिन पूवा मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों की सूची तैयार की िाएगी और सूची की प्रजतजलजपयों को सोसाइटी के कारबार के मूल स्ट् थान और इसकी सभी िाखाओं, यदि कोई हो, के नोरटस बोडा पर जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख के न्द् यूनतम पंरह दिन पूवा चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस सूची में जनम् नजलजखत जवजनर्िाष् ट होंगे - (क) सिस्ट् य का िाजखला संख् या और नाम, जपता या पजत का नाम, और व्यजिक की ििा में ऐसे सिस्ट् य का पता; और

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।
